approvalText: I approve all five ME-5 relationships, their identified PMIDs/DOIs, and the proposition-specific publication guards above for local-only, fail-closed implementation against baseline 16dbdc93bd4f2650829d46f64d567845f50c81d5; all five sources enter verified:false / pending-verification, with no citation promotion or remote writes.

rows.citation: Hansen S, Schwarz P, Rumessen J, Linneberg A, Kårhus LL. Osteoporosis and bone fractures in patients with celiac disease: A nationwide cohort study. Bone. 2023;177:116913. PMID 37730081. doi:10.1016/j.bone.2023.116913.
rows.publicationGuard: Require documented celiac disease and separately established osteoporosis. Treat the source as population-level association/risk evidence rather than proof that celiac disease caused osteoporosis in an individual. Preserve age, sex/menopausal status, body mass, vitamin D/calcium status, glucocorticoid exposure, smoking, endocrine or renal disease, and other established osteoporosis causes or contributors.

rows.citation: Li JQ, Welchowski T, Schmid M, et al. Prevalence, incidence and future projection of diabetic eye disease in Europe: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Eur J Epidemiol. 2020;35(1):11-23. PMID 31515657. doi:10.1007/s10654-019-00560-z.
rows.publicationGuard: Require established type 1 diabetes mellitus and separately established diabetic retinopathy by appropriate ophthalmic evaluation. Treat the source as population-level prevalence/complication evidence, not automatic individual causation or permission to infer retinopathy from diabetes alone. Preserve diabetes duration, glycemic control, hypertension, nephropathy, smoking, and other retinal or vascular contributors.

rows.citation: Ruffenach G, Hong J, Vaillancourt M, Medzikovic L, Eghbali M. Pulmonary hypertension secondary to pulmonary fibrosis: clinical data, histopathology and molecular insights. Respir Res. 2020;21(1):303. PMID 33208169. doi:10.1186/s12931-020-01570-2.
rows.publicationGuard: Require documented pulmonary fibrosis and a separately established diagnosis of pulmonary hypertension under accepted clinical/hemodynamic criteria. Do not infer pulmonary hypertension from dyspnea, hypoxemia, reduced DLCO, or a nonspecific echocardiographic estimate alone. Preserve other pulmonary-hypertension causes and groups, including left-heart disease, chronic thromboembolic disease, sleep-disordered breathing, drugs/toxins, and other lung diseases.

rows.citation: Hung JH, Hu LY, Tsai SJ, et al. Risk of psychiatric disorders following polycystic ovary syndrome: a nationwide population-based cohort study. PLoS One. 2014;9(5):e97041. PMID 24816764. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0097041.
rows.publicationGuard: Require documented polycystic ovary syndrome and a separately established depressive disorder. Treat the study as population-level temporal association/risk evidence, not proof of direct individual causation. Preserve obesity and insulin resistance, infertility, hyperandrogenic symptoms, sleep disturbance, psychosocial factors, medication or treatment effects, and independent psychiatric risk factors as potential contributors.

rows.citation: Cowan AJ, Green DJ, Kwok M, et al. Diagnosis and Management of Multiple Myeloma: A Review. JAMA. 2022;327(5):464-477. PMID 35103762. doi:10.1001/jama.2022.0003.
rows.publicationGuard: Require documented multiple myeloma and separately established anemia. The source supports anemia as a common myeloma manifestation but does not establish that every anemia in a patient with myeloma is attributable to the malignancy. Preserve chronic kidney disease, blood loss, nutritional deficiency, hemolysis, treatment-related marrow suppression, other marrow disorders, and other anemia etiologies as competing or contributing explanations.
